capture_method: Actual browser screenshots with separate manual review

visible_labels: How new calls are numbered. Changing the pattern never renumbers calls that already have a number.

How call numbers are written, for example FD-2026-0153: fixed text plus the YYYY or YY, MM, DD and SEQ tokens. The sequence starts again whenever the date it writes changes. Until a pattern is saved, calls keep the YY-SEQ numbers Resgrid has always issued.

Fixed text (letters, digits, - _ . /) around tokens: {YYYY} or {YY} the year, {MM} the month, {DD} the day and {SEQ} the sequence, which must appear once. The sequence starts again at 1 whenever the date in the number changes: each year with a year, each month with {MM}, each day with {DD}, and never without a date. {MM} needs a year and {DD} needs {MM}. Dates use the department's time zone.
Pads the sequence with leading zeros, so 4 writes 0153. 1 writes it without padding, as Resgrid always has.
Digits in the SEQ part of the call number, zero-padded: 4 writes 0153. 1 to 8 digits, 1 for no padding; changing it keeps the sequence's next number.

Month the numbering year starts, for calls numbered by a fiscal year. A yearly pattern starts again at 1 on that month and day, and YYYY and YY write the fiscal year's name; patterns with MM or DD follow the calendar. Unset is January, the calendar year.

For calls numbered by a fiscal year, pick the day it starts. A yearly pattern starts again at 1 that day, and {YYYY} and {YY} write the fiscal year's name. Most fiscal years are named by the year they end in, so one starting November 1, 2026 is 2027. January 1 is the calendar year. Patterns with {MM} or {DD} always follow the calendar.

For departments continuing numbers issued before Resgrid: the next call receives this sequence. It can only be raised, never lowered, so a number is never issued twice. Leave it blank to keep the current sequence.
captures.state: Read-only Call Settings reference showing its separate numbering year start; no call settings values changed or saved.
captures.label_observation_method: Actual CSS-visible DOM text and painted input values, within viewport and ancestor clips. Icon names/roles/rects are DOM observations. Separate image review must remove occlusion and bind hashes before use.
